key_insight: CARE (Confidence-Adaptive Routing of Experts) uses the router’s own output distribution as a confidence signal, sending more experts to uncertain tokens and fewer to easy ones. This makes Mixture-of-Experts LoRA more efficient without treating every token the same.
problem_solved: Standard MoE LoRA routes every token to a fixed number of experts k, which wastes compute on easy tokens and may under-serve difficult ones. The paper addresses the lack of token-wise adaptability in expert routing.
method: Interpret the router’s probability distribution as a per-token uncertainty estimate: peaked = confident, flat = uncertain.
Adapt the number of activated experts based on confidence instead of using a fixed k for all tokens.
Spend computation where ambiguity is highest, allocating more experts to hard tokens and fewer to easy tokens.
impact: For practitioners, this can improve compute efficiency while preserving or improving model quality on difficult inputs. It also offers a simple, principled way to make LoRA-based MoE models more dynamic and cost-aware.

paper_title: Spend Experts Where You Are Unsure: Confidence-Adaptive Routing for Mixture-of-Experts LoRA
paper_authors: Tom Saliencro, Rohan Desai, Priya Nair, Maya Lindqvist, Daniel Whitmore
